Chapter 3: Adjust Your Approach Based on Feedback
Picture this—you’ve put your heart and soul into a project, and now, you’re getting feedback. Maybe it’s from your team, your customers, or even your friends. How do you make the most of it?
Here’s the thing: feedback isn’t just about hearing what you did right or wrong. It’s like having a built-in GPS for your journey. Sometimes, it points out a shortcut you never saw coming. Other times, it lets you know you’ve veered off course, giving you a chance to get back on track.
So, how do you actually adjust your approach? First, listen with an open mind. Even if the feedback stings a little, it’s usually coming from a place of wanting to help you grow. Ask yourself, “What can I learn from this?” Instead of getting defensive, try to see the bigger picture.
Next, look for patterns. If several people mention the same thing, it’s probably worth paying extra attention to. For example, if your clients keep saying your emails are hard to follow, maybe it’s time to simplify your messaging.
Now, don’t be afraid to experiment. Adjust one thing at a time and see how it goes. Think of it like tweaking a recipe—maybe you add a little more spice, or try a new ingredient. Give yourself permission to make small changes, and watch for the results.
Here’s something to remember: adjusting your approach doesn’t mean you have to lose your unique voice or vision. It’s about blending what makes you, you—with insights that can make your work even stronger.
In the real world, some of the most successful people constantly adapt based on feedback. Athletes watch game footage to improve, businesses tweak their products after customer reviews, and even musicians fine-tune their sound based on audience reactions.
So, the next time you get feedback, see it as an opportunity. Take what’s useful, make a few adjustments, and keep moving forward. Growth isn’t about being perfect—it’s about being willing to learn, adapt, and try again.
Ready to turn feedback into your secret weapon? Let’s keep going.
